title: Strings
description: Create, combine, slice, and format text in Python.

lesson.title: Strings
lesson.summary: Work with text: indexing, slicing, methods, and f-strings.
lesson.body:
## Making strings

A **string** is a sequence of characters. Write one with single or double quotes (they behave the same):

```python
greeting = "hello"
name = 'Ada'
```

For text that spans several lines, use triple quotes:

```python
poem = """roses are red
violets are blue"""
```

## Combining text

Join strings with `+` and repeat with `*`:

```python
"foo" + "bar"   # "foobar"
"ab" * 3         # "ababab"
```

## Indexing and slicing

Characters are numbered from `0`. Negative indexes count from the end. A *slice* `s[start:stop]` includes `start` and excludes `stop`:

```python
s = "python"
s[0]     # "p"
s[-1]    # "n"
s[0:3]   # "pyt"
s[2:]    # "thon"
```

Strings are **immutable**: you can't change a character in place, but you can build a new string.

## Useful methods

Strings come with many built-in methods:

```python
"  hi  ".strip()     # "hi"   (remove surrounding whitespace)
"Ada".upper()         # "ADA"
"HELLO".lower()       # "hello"
"a,b,c".split(",")   # ['a', 'b', 'c']
"-".join(["a", "b"]) # "a-b"
```

## f-strings (the modern way to format)

Put an `f` before the quotes and embed expressions in `{}`:

```python
name = "Ada"
age = 30
print(f"{name} is {age} years old")   # Ada is 30 years old
print(f"Next year: {age + 1}")          # Next year: 31
```

f-strings are readable and fast — prefer them over `+` for building messages.

examples.title: Slice and dice
examples.description: Try changing the indexes and re-running.
examples.code:
s = "python"
print(s[0])      # p
print(s[-1])     # n
print(s[0:3])    # pyt
print(s[::-1])   # reversed: nohtyp

examples.title: Build a message with an f-string
examples.code:
name = "Ada"
items = 3
price = 2.5
total = items * price
print(f"{name}, your {items} items cost ${total:.2f}")

questions.prompt:
What does this print?

```python
s = "python"
print(s[1:4])
```
questions.explanation: Slice [1:4] includes index 1 and excludes 4, giving characters y, t, h.

questions.prompt: Which method removes whitespace from both ends of a string?

What does this print?

```python
name = "Ada"
print(f"Hi {name}!")
```
questions.explanation: An f-string evaluates `{name}` and inserts its value, "Ada".

questions.prompt: Strings in Python are immutable. What does that mean?
options: You cannot change a character in place; operations return new strings
questions.explanation: Immutable means the value can't be modified in place; methods produce new strings.
